title: Permission Journeys: Console Mini-Map & Cost Context Roles Explorer
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Design a compact, scan-friendly ‘Permission Journeys’ view in the Redwood Console that lets admins and platform owners quickly understand who has access to a resource, how role changes propagate across workspaces, and the cost implications of granting or removing roles. Scope includes: a mini-map overview of role scope, role-change diff preview, cost overlay per role, and an in-context audit timeline that surfaces access reviews and anomalies. Not in scope: full IAM policy editor or external identity provider sync flows. Background: current console RBAC surfaces are page-heavy; support tickets show admins often cannot triage cost spikes that correlate with permission changes. We need a lightweight UI for fast investigations and safer rollouts. Assumptions: workspaces and orgs already provide role metadata (role id, scope, permissions, linked cost center tags). Acceptance criteria: 1) Prototype demonstrates mini-map + detail panel interactions. 2) Design includes a role-change ‘what-if’ modal that estimates monthly token cost delta and impacted routes. 3) Usability test with 6 platform admins yields median SUS > 75 for task success (identify cause of an access-related cost spike). 4) Accessibility: color contrast and keyboard flows pass WCAG 2.1 AA. Key decisions and trade-offs: - Keep mini-map read-only to avoid accidental grants; edits are available in a guarded modal to surface approvals and audit requirements. This reduces accidental permission drift but adds an extra tap. - Cost overlay uses sampling of historical route/token usage rather than attempting real-time accounting; accurate enough for planning and keeps prototype performant. - Inline role previews use truncated permission lists with a ‘show all’ link to reduce cognitive load in the mini-map. Research & references: - Support tickets #SUP-1147 and #SUP-1189 show recurring incidents where role changes preceded cost anomalies. - Quantitative: 42% of admin flows are abandoned on deep permission pages (console analytics, Jan 2026). Deliverables: - Clickable Figma prototype (link in attachments). - Confluence PRD with rollout plan and audit requirements. - Annotated handoff for frontend engineering with component behaviour matrix. Metrics to watch post-launch: time-to-resolution for access-related incidents, number of role-change rollbacks, adoption of what-if modal, and % of role grants that include an explicit cost acknowledgement. Integration notes: - Hook into Console’s existing audit-log API to show role-change events in context; events must be correlated to cost data by route tag. - Security must sign off on the guarded modal flow and extra approval steps. Dependencies: ENG-49012 (audit-log correlation work), PM-224 (cost-center tagging enforcement), and runtime-1.20 (route-level tagging feature).
comments: 2026-02-21 - Kickoff: aligned with PM (Riley Moore) and Eng lead (Nina Alvarez). Agreed mini-map sits as a left rail and detail panel on the right.
2026-02-26 - Design review: tried three mini-map directions. Engineering prefers compact rows (performance reasons) so we iterated toward a condensed card layout.
2026-03-03 - Security review: flagged requirement for explicit approval step when granting workspace-level roles. Added guarded modal with audit copy and KMS audit hint.
2026-03-05 - Usability test plan approved. Recruiting 6 participants from customer-admin persona. Tasks focus on identifying the source of a token cost spike and drafting a mitigation plan.
2026-03-08 - PM feedback (Riley Moore): include a lightweight annotation feature in the audit timeline so admins can mark events as ‘investigated’ with a short note.
2026-03-09 - Engineering constraints: audit-log API currently returns events paginated; designed timeline to lazy-load and preserve scroll position to avoid jitter.
2026-03-10 - Current: Prototype submitted for stakeholder review. Next: incorporate usability test results and finalize component spec for frontend handoff.
